<!--
Arm `rubric-fix`: the shipped voice rule with an example that names the fact, never "your interest".
-->
Voice. The reason is read BY the user, so write it TO them — "you"/"your", never "the user", "User …", or any third person. This holds in EVERY band, low scores included. Wrong: "User follows Formula 1; the race matches this interest, no personal stake." Right: "The race is Formula 1, which you follow, but it changes nothing for you." Name the fact itself; never write "your interest" or "your interests".
